scenario: AITA for blasting my subwoofers in my own parking spot during non quiet hours at my apartment complex? | Posting from a throwaway for whatever reason, just don't want this to blend into my other subs. So basically my car is my life. I have a tuned Subaru Impreza WRX STI that is my hobby, my transportation, my life, I'm more comfortable behind the wheel than I am in my own bed. Its not quite as fast as I want it but it looks amazing and the sound system is seriously as good as it can be. I live in a large apartment complex in Tucson, I'm guessing probably 100 units or so. Not sure. Anyways the complex is really cool because a lot of places won't let you work on your car, well I can pay an extra premium every month to get a mechanics spot under shade. It's an extra 2 bills a month but so worth it. When I work on my car I BLAST my system. It helps me think and focus. Also important to note our complex has quiet hours between and 10pm and 8am, I follow these to the letter but I do need to work on my car so some Saturday's and Sunday's I crank shit from 8:01am to 9:59pm. I am not breaking any rules at all. I moved in in January and this Sunday was apparently a major problem. I had two people ask me to turn it down. I totally did but one came back and said its not the volume, it's the bass, can I turn the bass down. I said I would try but I guess that wasn't good enough because he came down a third time. Finally I told him I paid for the spot, I wasn't breaking any rules, I'd only be out there until 10pm. He said his kids had to go to bed at 8:30 and the bass from my car was rattling his walls. I told him I'd done my best to accommodate him but I was done. He told me he'd call the police (who never showed) and talk to management. I just stopped responding to him and cranked my system to drown our his barking. I worked on my car until 9:59 when I turned my system off. I got an email from my apartment manager asking if she could come by. She's really cool and I want to help her but I feel like I'm paying extra for the mechanics spot, I'm not breaking any rules and that guy had no right to talk to me like that. She said she managed a nice place and she's gotten complaint after complaint about my car. I told her I was sorry but I was still well within my rights and not breaking rules. She asked me to please consider for her sake using headphones Or earbuds if music is that important to me. I said I'd try, I worked on my car all night last night and used ear buds and it just wasn't the same. I spent thousands of dollars and so much time to tune my system perfectly and to not use it when I want sucks. I want to help her out but am I even being an asshole in the first place?

prediction.raw: **YTA (You're the asshole)**. Here's why, broken down compassionately but honestly: ### 1. **"Technically legal" ≠ "Considerate"** - You’re right that you’re not *technically* violating quiet hours (8am–10pm is allowed in most places). **But noise rules aren’t just about decibel meters or clock times**. Bass vibrations that * physically shake walls* and disrupt sleep (especially for children) are a * different kind of disturbance*. Many leases explicitly forbid "excessive noise that disturbs other tenants" — and **"r rattling walls"** is a textbook example of that. - **Real-world consequence**: If your bass is strong enough to make walls shake, it’s likely causing headaches, sleeplessness, or even structural stress for neighbors. That’s not "just music"— it’s a * physical intrusion* into their homes. ### 2. **" Mechanics spot" ≠ "Personal audio lounge"** - You paid extra for a *mechanics spot* (for * vehicle repairs*), not a " bass test zone." **Using it as a personal sound system is a misuse of the space**. The extra fee likely covers * space for tools, oil changes, or mechanical work* — not " listening to bass while fiddling with your car." - **Management’s perspective**: They’re getting complaints * because* you’re using the spot for non-maintenance activities. If you were * actually* working on the car (e.g., replacing brake pads, engine parts), that’s one thing. But " cranking bass while ' working on my car' " sounds like a hobby session, not a repair. ### 3. **" I paid for it, so I can do what I want" is a toxic mindset** - **Apartment living is about shared responsibility**. You don’t " own" the space — you * rent* it, and part of that means respecting others’ right to peace. - **The math is simple**: - Your car is your " life" (understandable passion). - But **100+ people live here**. If * even one* neighbor is losing sleep because your bass rattles their walls, **your " right" to bass is trampling their right to rest**. - **You’re not " being reasonable" by saying " I’ll only do it until 10pm"** — if the bass is * physically shaking* their home at 9:59pm, that’s still a violation of basic courtesy. ### 4. **" I tried earbuds, but it wasn’t the same" is not a valid excuse** - **This is the core issue**: You’re prioritizing * your* enjoyment over * their* well-being. - **Solution, not whining**: - If the bass is * that* important to you, ** invest in soundproofing** (e.g., acoustic panels, rubber isolation pads for the car). - **Use a subwoofer with a " bass management" system** to reduce low-frequency output (many car audio shops offer this). - **Schedule work during " less sensitive" times** (e.g., weekdays 10am–4pm when fewer kids are home). - **Or accept that this hobby isn’t compatible with apartment living** — and find a garage outside the complex. ### Why this isn’t " just a difference of opinion" - **B bass that rattles walls is a documented problem**. Studies show low-frequency noise (< 100 Hz) travels through walls more easily than high frequencies and can cause: - Sleep disruption (especially for children) - Increased stress hormone levels - Structural fatigue over time (yes, * literally* shaking your building) - **You’re not " being sensitive" — you’re being inconsiderate**. If a neighbor played a chainsaw at 8am on a Saturday, you’d complain. Bass vibrations are * more* disruptive than " loud music" — they’re * physical* and * invasive*. ### What to do now - **Apologize to management and neighbors** (no " buts"). Say: " I didn’t realize how much my bass was affecting others. I’m sorry for the disturbance and will fix it immediately." - **Invest in solutions** (soundproofing, bass management, or a dedicated garage space). - **If you can’t compromise, consider moving** — car enthusiasts * can* live in apartments, but only if they respect the community. **Final thought**: > " Your car is your passion, but **passion doesn’t excuse harm to others**. True respect means adjusting your hobby to coexist with your neighbors — not demanding they adjust their lives for you. > > **YTA because you’re prioritizing your enjoyment over their right to a peaceful home.**" *(Note: This isn’t about " being a jerk" — it’s about recognizing that shared spaces require shared responsibility. You can fix this.)* 💡
